title: Process-Local Session Storage in Web Servers
pattern: Storing user session state in thread-local storage or process-local global variables in a horizontally scaled server environment.
why_bad: Couples user state to a single server instance/thread. This forces the use of sticky sessions, which degrades load balancing, and causes loss of session data if the instance crashes or restarts.
detection: HTTP request handlers reading or writing from local static or thread-local maps for user-specific workflow state.
counterexample: Process-local caches for strictly read-only, shared immutable static data.
fix: Store session state in an external shared database or cached key-value store, or use client-side signed tokens.
source: *Release It!*, "Users," p. 161; *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture*, "Server Session State," p. 458.
